prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text: Our allowance for credit losses ("ACL") is maintained at a level necessary to absorb the current expected credit losses. Management, in determining the allowance for credit losses, considers historic losses and changes in the nature and volume of loan activities, along with the general economic and real estate market conditions. A description of our methodology in establishing our allowance for credit losses is set forth in the section “ Management ’ s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of SR Bancorp — Critical Accounting Policies-Allowance for Credit Losses ” in our Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2026 and in this Form 10-Q. The allowance for credit losses as of September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026 were maintained at levels that represent management’s best estimate of current expected losses in the loan portfolio. However, this analysis process is inherently subjective, as it requires us to make estimates that are susceptible to revisions as more information becomes available.

nonint.text: We recognize interest and/or penalties related to income tax matters in other operating expenses.

nonop.text: Interest Expense. Interest expense increased $1.1 million, or 24.3%, to $5.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $4.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $109.2 million increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities. The increase in the average balance was primarily due to an increase of $75.5 million, or 22.6%, in the average balance of interest-bearing demand deposits, a $25.2 million, or 9.3%, increase in the average balance of certificates of deposit due to the acquisition of $50.0 million in brokered deposits and a $23.2 million, or 66.9%, increase in the average balance of borrowings for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, partially offset by a decrease of $14.7 million in the average balance of savings and club accounts. The increase in interest expense was also due to a 33 basis point increase in the average rate of interest-bearing demand deposits to 2.20% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 1.87% for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting from competitively priced rates, partially offset by a 59 basis point decrease in the average rate on Federal Home Loan Bank borrowings from 4.39% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 3.80% for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

tax.text: Income Tax Expense. The provision for income taxes was $362,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $202,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The Company’s effective tax rate was 25.3% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 22.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to an increase in non-deductible expenses.

ocf.text: Our cash flows are derived from operating activities, investing activities and financing activities as reported in our Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows included in our Consolidated Financial Statements.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income. Net interest income increased $707,000, or 9.3%, to $8.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $7.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest rate spread increased one basis point to 2.57% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 2.56% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest margin decreased two basis points to 3.03% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 3.05% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest-earning assets decreased $10.0 million, or 4.6%, to $209.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $219.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the Company’s net interest rate spread was primarily a result of an increase in the yield on interest-earning assets slightly exceeding the increase in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income increased $37,000, or 6.5%, to $602,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $565,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to gain on sale of loans of $42,000 in 2026, partially offset by a decrease in the other income of $24,000.

intro.text: SR Bancorp, Inc. SR Bancorp, Inc. (“SR Bancorp” or the “Company”) is a Maryland chartered company and the holding company for Somerset Regal Bank (the “Bank”). SR Bancorp’s primary business activity is the ownership of the outstanding common stock of Somerset Regal Bank. SR Bancorp does not own or lease any property but instead uses the premises, equipment and other property of Somerset Regal Bank with the payment of appropriate rental fees, as required by applicable law and regulations, under the terms of an expense allocation agreement.
